selected_primary_idea.title: Relativistic Mission Envelope: a coupled subluminal feasibility frontier
selected_primary_idea.summary: Compute a provenance-preserving feasible region over beta, payload, propulsion, braking, shielding, and operations rather than presenting a cruise speed in isolation.
selected_primary_idea.research_object: A massive robotic or crewed spacecraft travelling between specified stellar systems under established relativity.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: The relativistic energy divergence, beam or onboard propulsion limits, braking closure, ISM impact environment, shielding mass, and operational constraints jointly restrict beta.
selected_primary_idea.hypothesis: A coupled model yields a narrower and better calibrated feasible region than energy-only or travel-time-only screening.
falsification_conditions: A validated self-consistent mission lies outside the predicted infeasible region using the same stated payload and environment assumptions.
Joint constraints do not improve held-out mission-architecture prediction relative to an energy-only baseline.
A verified shielding or braking architecture changes the controlling high-beta failure mode without the predicted mass or energy trade-off.
selected_primary_idea.claim_boundary: The direction does not claim observed flight, a new physical law, exact light-speed travel, or faster-than-light travel.

rejected_ideas.title: Assume a warp or reactionless drive
rejected_ideas.reason: No verified evidence in the frozen Survey supports using such a mechanism as a mission premise.
